main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). A triangular-shaped Mid North Coast track with tight, sweeping turns and a 350m home straight. The tight triangular geometry generates a distinct early speed ('E') and on-pace presser ('P') bias. The Kikuyu grass surface holds together remarkably well during rain compared to inland tracks.
main_turf.post_bias: INSIDE BARRIER BIAS: Inside barriers (stalls 1–5) hold a distinct advantage across all sprint distances (1000m to 1400m). Outer draws (9+) must expend significant early energy to cross over or risk being trapped wide on tight turns.

handicapping_angles.triangular_speed_bias: Because of the triangular layout and tight corners, pure front-runners ('E' types) and prominent stalkers have a significant edge. Downgrade deep closers ('Swoopers') unless drawn inside to save ground.
handicapping_angles.kikuyu_wet_track_durability: Taree's dense Kikuyu grass surface drains exceptionally well and handles rain better than standard bush tracks. Soft/Heavy tracks often play slightly firmer than official track ratings suggest.
handicapping_angles.hunter_and_provincial_shippers: Taree attracts high-volume shippers from Newcastle, Port Macquarie, and Scone (e.g. Kris Lees, Nathan Doyle, Colt Prosser). Upgrade runners dropping back from Newcastle/Wyong provincial grade (+3.0 pts).
handicapping_angles.taree_cup_showcase_class: During the August Taree Cup ($100k+ Showcase) feature meeting, race quality elevates to Provincial level.
